alt: Poster: Which NAV will your purchase get? Cut-off 3:00 pm (liquid and overnight funds purchases 1:30 pm); funds must be available by cut-off; late funds get a later business day's NAV; redemptions have no funds-availability condition
text:
A mutual fund purchase is priced on when your money is available, not only when you click.

Under SEBI's applicable-NAV rules (AMFI summary, in force since 1 Feb 2021 for schemes other than liquid and overnight funds), a purchase or switch-in gets that day's NAV only if the application is received by 3:00 pm on a business day and the full amount is available for use by 3:00 pm the same day. SIP instalments are purchases and follow the same rule.

If the application is in time but the funds arrive after 3:00 pm, the NAV is that of the first later business day on which funds are available before 3:00 pm. An application after 3:00 pm with funds in by 3:00 pm gets the next business day's NAV. For liquid and overnight funds, the subscription cut-off is 1:30 pm. Redemptions and switch-outs have a 3:00 pm cut-off and no funds-availability condition.

Our reading: for clients, payment timing matters as much as order timing, especially for lump sums made through slower payment modes. This is an opinion, not advice.

For practitioners: where do you most often see NAV-date surprises, lump sums, SIP debits or switches?
